intro.headline: Your hosts, your keys, your history — all on this machine.
intro.body: Sessions, credentials and the commands you have run are kept here, encrypted with a passphrase only you hold. No account, no sync, no telemetry. Make a session, confirm the host key on the first connection, then work in a terminal or in the file workbench beside it.
intro.notice: This page names no host and counts nothing: no session, no host key and no history is shown on it.

sessions.title: Session library
sessions.body: Address, authentication, jump hosts and forwards in one saved entry, with groups to keep them apart.

terminal.title: Real terminals
terminal.body: A terminal per session, with its own font and colour scheme — and one command that can be sent to several at once.

files.title: File workbench
files.body: Both directories side by side, drag to move a file, and one packed archive when a whole tree is going over.

monitor.title: Host monitor
monitor.body: Load, memory, disk and processes, sampled over the connection you already have — nothing to install on the host.

actions.title: Common operations
actions.tip: The library is on the left as well: expand a group, or right-click a session to edit it, open its files or copy its address.

start.title: Getting started
start.stepSession: Create a session: address, authentication, and any jump hosts on the way.
start.stepHostKey: Confirm the host key on the first connection. A key that has changed stops the connection instead of asking twice.
start.stepTerminal: Open a terminal, or the file workbench beside it.
start.pending: Sessions, password and key authentication and terminals work today; jump hosts, forwarding, SFTP and the platform agents do not yet. A session can only reach a host this build speaks to directly.

status.title: What this build can and cannot do
status.note: Read from the descriptors — the same tables Rust compiles. A capability is only claimed once the code behind it exists.
